edges.effect_quant: CBT is one of the better-supported tinnitus interventions for reducing tinnitus-related distress and quality-of-life burden. The Cochrane review of 28 randomized studies found benefit on tinnitus impact compared with usual care or other comparators, and newer umbrella and expert reviews continue to place CBT among the most consistently supported management strategies.
edges.population: adults with chronic bothersome tinnitus undergoing cognitive behavioral therapy
edges.mechanism: CBT does not silence the sound itself so much as change threat appraisal, attentional fixation, avoidance behavior, and downstream anxiety or depressive responses that amplify tinnitus suffering.
edges.summary: This is a strong symptom-burden edge. CBT reliably helps people cope better with tinnitus and reduces distress, even though it does not necessarily eliminate the auditory percept itself.
edges.caveats: Benefit is strongest for distress and tinnitus-related quality of life, not necessarily loudness. Delivery format, therapist skill, and comorbid anxiety or depression can all shape the magnitude of improvement.
